spillover_issues.body:
Earlier cohort experiment (held): 32 tasks and 31 accepted teacher traces; SFT pending. A student failed
one BixBench question through cohort-selection errors; this is not a benchmark score.
See the [experiment record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9257#issuecomment-5781700724).
Revalidate existing artifacts under the stronger contracts below.

The [authoring checkpoint](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/a55f80f08a876bd87dc39e5301042dc65092e73f)
registers **140 recipes with one task each by default** across 13 domains.
There are **25 real-data candidates** and 115 synthetic correctness controls.
Controls are for verifier development and do not count toward the final training
release. Real inputs include the full GSE60450 RNA-seq matrix, deposited mmCIF
structures, three complete annotated phage genomes, observed ENA ERR266411 read
pairs, curated UniProt globin and COX1 proteins, and published Mayo PBC baseline and
longitudinal records. The [provenance manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/data_sources.json)
retains accessions, licenses, hashes and transformations. The latest task-generation
and environment suite passes 450 tests, including cached input access, byte-preserving
serialization and rejection of corrupted cache content. Tree checks cover complete
identities, unrooted topology and branch lengths while accepting equivalent rooting
and Newick order. Another 64 focused artifact tests pass, including complete
MatrixMarket counts, entry-order invariance, gzip corruption and changed counts
with correct summaries. Full-study MatrixMarket verifier performance remains
unmeasured; numerical and artifact contracts remain explicit.

**37 of 50 packages have passing native checks:** 34 on three reference cases each,
and IQ-TREE, FastTree and RAxML on one shared observed COX1 alignment.
[Execution evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/native_validation.json)
retains resolved environments, commands, input/output hashes, grades and earlier
failures. Picard and fastp passed on observed reads; MAFFT and MUSCLE passed on
real proteins. Recent runs use CPUs on a reserved TRC host in `us-central2` and
regional GCS. Constrain reserved hosts and verify placement to avoid paid CPU
fallback. Thirteen repositories still need executable references. Package checks
do not establish full ID workflows. A separate
[Harbor record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/container_validation.json)
records passing batches of 21 oracle cases and nine correctly rejected negative
controls across nine recipes, with no model calls or remaining validation sandboxes.
Those results apply to the recorded task and grader hashes.

The connected GSE60450 differential-expression and GO-enrichment workflows pass
six native R reference cases with complete intermediate tables and negative
controls. Their [native record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bc7171111b4bcebd44c68befbcd2cdbd43e58210/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/native_validation_runs/e39ec1c86f62.json)
contains hashes and the pinned DESeq2 environment. Both canonical workflows now
pass in Harbor, and both controls with changed intermediate tables and correct
summaries fail. Oracle execution took 9.3 and 20.3 seconds respectively; these are
reference runtimes, not teacher latency. All four trials reported the Haswell
BLAS kernel and cleanup left no sandboxes. The [container record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e2f0ad4d9e07230cf7c9e0f87e13bf29eca57643/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/container_validation.json)
preserves the successful cases and earlier failure. A controlled kernel comparison
reproduced the probability-field mismatch with Sandy Bridge; selecting Haswell
fixed it without changing tolerances. The canonical 140-task corpus rebuilt in
18.7 minutes on reserved TRC CPUs with every oracle, permutation check and negative
control passing. Its verified archive is preserved in regional GCS beyond Iris
retention. The inspection snapshot is pinned to `4b3188238f` with 1,241 ID records;
the latest versioned inventory below has 1,449, including BAISBench and the newer
tree-component mappings. The browser snapshot and current inventory retain
separate revisions.

The [agentic benchmark inventory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_sources.json)
records all 48 benchmark/protocol rows from the spreadsheet's **Agentic (Harbor)
tab only**: 42 provisional ID and six OOD. Protocol variants and subsets overlap.
Preserve every OOD assignment: Terminal-Bench-Science (full/lite), GeneBench
(original/Pro), BioMysteryBench and SciCode.

The [task-level index](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_coverage.json)
links [per-benchmark task inventories](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_tasks)
with **1,449 provisional-ID records across twenty-one releases**. Forty-six have
component mappings, 1,402 are unmapped and one is excluded from authoring; none is
workflow-validated. BAISBench adds 193 discovery questions across 41 studies and
15 annotation dataset identities. All question stems have assessed workflow
patterns; Task1 scoring and input schemas remain uninspected. BioML's released experiment selects 24 definitions; its configured-ID duplicates, invalid YAML,
shared patterns and pending individual reviews are explicit. Definitions and
protocol variants are not independent workflow counts. Released examples and
authorized gated metadata are distinguished from advertised full suites.
Nineteen eligible BixBench3 prompts and all 131 required output artifacts have been
reviewed for workflow stages, identities, row universes and units; the excluded
objective retains an identifier only. BioMysteryBench retains 90 identifiers only,
without patterns or training mappings. The [inventory guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_tasks/README.md)
explains coverage states and how incomplete releases are recorded.

The COX1 tree measurements now map to 18 BixBench endpoints and five overlapping
Verified-50 protocols. Those 23 component mappings share one biological input;
cross-gene/group aggregation, native PhyKIT agreement and benchmark-lineage
screening remain missing. Method replicates are not biological replicates.

Each versioned inventory records IDs, patterns, stages, formats, recipe mappings,
validation evidence and gaps. Shared capsule, claim, insight, assay and original-question
identities preserve overlaps. Source partitions do not create additional dataset
splits. Source grading also needs assessment: some protocols use simulated
observations or activity proxies, and public assay labels mean that prediction
scores alone cannot establish correct cross-validation. Detailed denominators,
scorer limitations and per-task review status stay in the linked files.

The connected COX1 workflow passes native validation on reserved TRC CPUs.
Its 94 unchanged curated proteins have 89 distinct sequences in a fixed 558-column
MAFFT alignment; a complete accession map preserves the duplicate identities.
The input-reading oracle reran IQ-TREE, FastTree and standard RAxML in **17.1 minutes**.
An independent Biopython calculation checks all three complete trees, 3,916 pairwise
distance rows and three unrooted RF comparisons. All ten missing/changed-artifact
controls fail. The [native evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/native_validation_runs/e2f647365a6f.json)
records exact packages, commands, hashes and the shared single biological case.
Earlier time-cap failures remain recorded. The Harbor oracle passed in **622.3
seconds** with unchanged tolerances; the changed-tree and missing-distance-row
controls both received zero despite correct summaries. No model calls ran. The
enclosing worker failed during a redundant sandbox deletion (HTTP 409, state
change in progress). An independent paginated check confirmed no owned sandboxes
remained; the run record retains that cleanup failure separately from the passing
validation. Biological source-independence review remains pending; a single
mitochondrial gene does not establish species-tree truth.

Full GSE81682 source preparation passed an exact count-and-order round trip:
**1,920 cells, 46,078 endogenous features, 92 ERCC controls and 22,590,142 nonzero
counts**. HTSeq mapping metrics remain separate. The 76 MB compressed MatrixMarket
file and metadata are preserved in regional GCS with hashes in the provenance
manifest. The builder now accepts original binary/compressed files from an explicit
hash-checked cache; no input reduction is required to fit Git.

The GEO metadata has 3,840 sample records, including additional Rep labels. Its
extraction description names 20 mice, while the paper Methods describe 10 with
pooling; no donor/pool mapping to the 1,920 columns has been established. Broad
sorting gates and fine cell annotations remain distinct. This source is not yet
a registered task; scientific contracts, redistribution terms and full benchmark
lineage review remain open.

The [coverage assessment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-task-catalog.md#id-workflow-coverage-and-input-realism)
and inspection browser expose the counts, examples, provenance and reference
results. Metadata inspection does not count as implemented coverage.

**The current deliverable is the final executable task dataset.** Completion
requires broad coverage of eligible agentic ID benchmarks' scientific workflows on real
biological inputs, actual tool execution across all 50 repositories, private
executable oracles for every task, validated offline Harbor environments,
scientific contracts and benchmark-lineage exclusions. Target all-real training
data; document any necessary exception. Keep synthetic correctness controls
outside the training release. Preserve one train split and use one reviewed task
per recipe by default; neither 100 recipes nor the current task count is a cap. Assess every
accessible ID task and report complete workflows, components and gaps separately.

The collection remains under development. Full scientific review, container
validation and artifact-lineage screening are pending. Teacher collection is a
later phase, not a completion condition for this task dataset; no model calls have
run on this task collection. The separate cohort/SFT experiment above remains on
hold; this work does not restart GPU training.

Generate computational-biology training tasks and teacher trajectories for
supervised fine-tuning (SFT), grounded by default in real biological datasets.
Package executable Harbor tasks with independently established reference results.
Validated tasks can also supply binary rewards for reinforcement learning (RL).

Test generation quality/cost and transferable analysis skills. This issue defines
the program; individual experiments specify models, scale, and budgets.

## Design decisions

- Use executable checks for task acceptance, trajectory selection, rewards, and
  evaluation. Models may author recipes, instructions, code, and solutions;
  acceptance must not depend on LLM-as-a-judge. Review scientific assumptions once
  per recipe version, then validate instances programmatically.
- Make connected workflows the main training unit. Start at a meaningful analysis
  boundary and require dependent stages: for example, count matrix → sample join
  → fitted biological contrast → multiple-testing correction → enrichment.
  Preserve sample identity, units, eligibility, biological replication and
  uncertainty. Check intermediate artifacts and the final result; a scientifically material upstream
  error must affect downstream acceptance. Retain focused component tasks for
  skill practice and verifier diagnostics. Fit the workflow within 30 minutes.
- Exercise scientific operations and actual tools across the full 50-repository
  inventory, supplementing gaps such as imaging. Keep reference scripts that run
  each package on task inputs and check its results against the independent
  contract. Record versions, commands, input hashes, outputs, and verdicts.
  Report package execution and scientific workflow coverage separately.
- Every task must have a private executable oracle solution. A recipe-level
  implementation may solve all its instances from their public inputs; it must
  never read the private expected answer. Run actual biological packages where
  appropriate and retain commands, versions and complete output artifacts. Keep
  oracles and references inaccessible to solving agents. Verify alternative valid
  outputs semantically and exercise plausible scientific mistakes: oracle success
  alone does not establish verifier correctness.
- Target real biological data for every task in the final training release.
  Document any necessary exception; keep synthetic correctness fixtures outside
  the training release. Select public,
  appropriately licensed datasets independent of the evaluation benchmarks, and
  retain accession/version, source URL, checksums, and every subsetting or
  preprocessing step. Use bounded subsets that preserve biological replication,
  sample structure, noise, sparsity, ambiguity, missingness, and native formats.
  Larger fabricated inputs alone do not satisfy this requirement. Keep tiny
  synthetic fixtures for correctness controls and explicitly labeled perturbations.
  Distinguish real, modified-real, and simulated inputs in metadata and inspection.
  Establish independently verified numerical or artifact references for the
  specified analysis on these observations.
  Grade large matrices, alignments, and call sets as native artifacts using bounded
  reads. Size tasks to the 30-minute attempt budget while retaining their workflow.
- Track coverage against individual tasks in every provisional ID agentic benchmark,
  alongside the repository, skill, and format inventories. Record which workflow
  stages and scientific decisions each training recipe exercises, with linked
  examples and validation evidence. A shared package or format does not establish
  task coverage; distinguish component practice from a validated dependent workflow.
- Source training inputs independently. Evaluation questions, answers, fixtures,
  and their teacher trajectories stay outside the generation and training corpus. Follow
  [Marin's evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193),
  including the stricter boundary around OOD questions and development scores.
- Build on Harbor and existing Marin components. Keep implementation on an
  experimental branch under `experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/`, containing the
  generators and inspection pages. A merge to `main` is
  not a prerequisite for experiments.

## Seeds, skills, and generation

A **recipe** defines the biological objective, input construction, output contract,
reference, and verifier. An **instance** supplies inputs and parameters. A **lineage**
groups a dataset and its derivatives, including perturbations, subsets, repairs,
and prompt variants. A **skill** should transfer across recipes and tools.

Use three authoring routes with the same admission rules:

1. **Grounded analysis:** extract a bounded operation from examples, tests, or
   downstream analyses; reconstruct its purpose and supply independent real
   biological inputs under the data policy above. Discover uses through imports,
   dependencies, commands, and workflows. Corroborate ambiguous
   command names; a text hit alone does not establish biological relevance.
2. **Skill-directed generation:** cover missing capabilities and combinations with
   cited methods and independent references. Vary strand, biological replicate,
   outcome coding, missingness, covariates, and enrichment universe. Renaming genes
   or changing random seeds alone does not broaden skill coverage.
3. **Workflow repair:** introduce a scientific defect in a working analysis: wrong
   sample join, contrast, denominator, or coordinates. The reference must pass and
   the defective workflow fail on verified inputs. Score repaired biological outputs,
   allowing equivalent code changes.

Freeze the semantic contract before paraphrasing instructions: population, units,
decision, schema, and any method choice needed for a unique answer. Leave other
implementation choices open. Expand reviewed recipes with templates; model calls
are not required for each instance. Changed assumptions require a new recipe version.

The sequence is **recipe review → inputs and reference → validation → Harbor task
→ teacher attempts → successful-trace export**. Teacher failure does not invalidate
a task with a working reference; retain difficult instances and failures for analysis.

[On Data Engineering for Scaling LLM Terminal Capabilities](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21193v1)
motivates seed/skill generation and shared environments. Its Qwen3-8B skill result
was 12.4% versus 6.18% for seeds, with unequal datasets (139,841 versus 124,366
examples) and weak scientific-computing performance. It motivates a biology
comparison, without establishing a controlled advantage for either route.

## Provisional ID benchmarks, OOD holdout and judge-free scoring

Use the versioned [agentic source inventory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_sources.json)
for provisional ID eligibility. It covers the spreadsheet's Agentic (Harbor) tab
only and preserves all existing OOD labels. OOD formulations and derivatives must
not guide training recipe authoring. Freeze eligible items, answer representations,
and adapter revisions before student comparison; disclose exclusions. Coverage
references need not supply a numerical score. Do not fill missing scores with LLM judgments.

Maintain a version-controlled inventory file per benchmark, indexed by the
coverage registry and inspection browser. List every publicly inspectable task and
its workflow pattern; distinguish advertised totals, public inventories,
unreleased items and protocol variants that share tasks. For each benchmark item, record its dataset revision and
stable task/question/workflow ID, required workflow stages and scientific decisions,
formats/tools, mapped training recipes and example IDs, independent data accessions,
executed reference evidence, runtime, and remaining gaps. Use explicit statuses:
`unmapped`, `component-only`, `composed-unvalidated`, `workflow-validated`, and
`restricted/excluded` with a reason. Mark a workflow validated only after its
connected stages and final artifacts pass on independent real biological data.
Report total and eligible task counts separately for each benchmark, preserving
unmapped and excluded items in the inventory. This measures training-workflow
coverage; it is not a benchmark performance score.

Use only metadata and descriptions permitted by each dataset's terms and Marin's
evaluation policy for this registry. Keep restricted questions, rubrics, answers,
and task formulations outside recipe authoring; record permitted IDs and the
restriction instead of silently omitting an item. In particular, BioMysteryBench's
evaluation-only content must not become an item-level recipe-generation source.

The original four ID sources have the following scoring constraints. The wider
source list and task inventories remain in the linked files.

| Benchmark | Coverage and scoring decision |
|---|---|
| [BixBench, `f8cc3bd`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/BixBench.jsonl) | 205 question IDs: expression, enrichment, phylogenetics, imaging, and other analyses. Use structured-answer MCQ with exact option comparison. Numeric open-answer subsets need published units/ranges and typed parsing. Report these variants separately. |
| [BioMysteryBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/BioMysteryBench-full/blob/main/README.md) | **OOD holdout.** Biological data reasoning. Terms restrict questions, rubrics, and task formulation to evaluation; exclude them from recipe authoring. Score only unambiguous typed rubric targets with independently validated references. Preserve allowed-domain and dataset-identification restrictions. |
| [CompBioBench, `86ee0a2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Genentech/compbiobench-data-v1/blob/86ee0a22e036fef2a98f382f8fd528d5d390dde3/compbiobench.v1.tsv) | 100 tasks; 78 flagged internet-required. The question table lacks answers, and the [runner](https://github.com/Genentech/compbiobench-runner/blob/dc350ed37ccd7d7ce96347d139f06dc4bf283f26/run_simple_benchmark.py) records responses rather than correctness. Use for coverage; independently referenced subsets may supply custom scores. |
| [BiomniBench-DA, `e1c8ca5`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/tree/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235) | All 50 instructions/configurations inspected: association, mutation, expression, and composition. Its [verifier](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/blob/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235/da-1-3/tests/llm_judge.py) uses an LLM. Adaptation requires numerical/artifact contracts and reproduced references; exclude free-form interpretation. |
| [BioAgent Bench, v4](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21800v4) | Ten workflows. Use a named result-only subset of the four marked verifiable: `cystic-fibrosis`, `giab`, `transcript-quant`, `viral-metagenomics`. Disable process judging and report per-task limitations. |

BixBench's [grader](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/blob/49311180bdacb324c596f2e07596c126f2004008/bixbench/graders.py)
compares MCQs deterministically, but open-answer `range_verifier` invokes an LLM,
as does its [trajectory postprocessing](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/blob/49311180bdacb324c596f2e07596c126f2004008/bixbench/postprocessing.py).
Parse explicit final answers directly, preserving numeric signs/decimals.

BioAgent's [taskset](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/tasksets/bioagent/bioagent_taskset/taskset.py)
calls a process judge; its [result scorer](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/tasksets/bioagent/bioagent_taskset/scoring.py)
has partial-overlap checks and an evolution check ignoring alleles. In the four-task
subset, viral detection does not verify every assembly output and transcript counts
require exact agreement. Preserve definitions for named subset results; strengthen
new training rewards. Changed protocols are adapter variants, not published scores.

## Skill inventory and sampling

Use the [skill inventory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-task-catalog.md#skills)
to cover sequence/interval reasoning, read and genotype QC, sample joins,
normalization, statistical design, enrichment, phylogeny, taxonomy, workflow repair,
and image measurements. Each entry specifies an independently checkable outcome.

Record primary/secondary skills, prerequisites, outcome, toolchain, and variations
in Marin's curriculum schema. Assign tags during recipe authoring; instance
acceptance needs no LLM routing. Sample families, recipes, and lineages uniformly
at each level; variants share their parent's weight. Give compositions one primary
family. Balance SFT loss-bearing tokens across eligible families and report gaps.

Include positive/null effects, confounding, unequal cell yields, missingness, decoys,
and explicitly invalid inputs. Pair invalid cases with valid ones so blanket
refusal fails. A null result is valid biology. Score fitted statistics for the
realized sample, not latent population parameters. Compositions must connect real
dependencies: aggregation → contrast → enrichment, or coordinates → consequences.
Separate supplied-intermediate analysis from full inference in coverage reports.

## Biological data formats

Make format literacy an explicit skill and coverage axis: read, validate, query,
write, and convert native files while preserving biological meaning. The
[format catalog](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-task-catalog.md#biological-data-formats)
covers BED/BED12, FASTA/FASTQ, SAM/BAM/CRAM, GFF3/GTF, VCF/BCF, PDB/mmCIF,
phylogenetic alignments/trees, sparse single-cell matrices, and imaging formats.

Exercise coordinates, strand, identifiers, quality encodings, CIGAR/flags,
ploidy/missing alleles, annotation relationships, structural models/alternate
locations, array axes/layers, units, and metadata retention. Supply native files
at declared sizes with pinned format profiles and offline documentation. Grade complete
biological records or semantic conversion equivalence against independent references;
parser success alone is insufficient. Record format profiles/operations in task
metadata and the browser. CSV/JSON proxies do not establish native-format coverage.

## Task diversity and realism

Use **one reviewed real-data task per recipe by default**. Expand distinct
scientific workflows before adding parameter variants. A recipe defines the
scientific problem, public inputs, workflow and executable contract; a task is a
concrete, reproducible instance. Additional instances are useful when another
organism, dataset, study design, modality or biological decision adds meaningful
coverage. Paraphrases, renamed records and random seeds do not count as new
recipes. Keep extra generated boundary and failure cases for validation without
requiring their inclusion in training.

There is **no fixed cap on tasks or recipes**. Expand wherever individual ID
benchmark workflows, skills, formats or repository operations reveal gaps. Make
connected workflows the main training unit, using observed biological variation,
realistic data volumes, native formats and scientifically meaningful decisions.
A focused component task remains useful when it represents actual analysis work.
Do not impose easy/medium/hard labels, quotas or sampling weights. Describe each
task by its biological question, study design, input scale, dependent stages,
required decisions, artifacts and measured runtime. Keep the 30-minute solve
limit and one correctness standard. More bytes or more steps alone do not justify
a task.

Keep a **single train split** and evaluate on the separate benchmarks. Choose
corpus sizes from coverage, validation quality and learning curves. Version
snapshots and report available and successfully solved task IDs separately.
Compare nested recipe-diverse sets as the corpus grows; fixed task counts do not
determine admission or completion.

## Reference and reward contract

Version each contract: artifacts/fields, IDs, units, population/denominators, methods,
equivalences, tolerances, and invalid-input behavior. Hidden tests may vary inputs
but must not introduce undisclosed scientific requirements. Choose an adequate reference:

- **Exact construction:** independent sequence/interval arithmetic, patient/cell
  ledgers, codon translation, or pixel sums. Check identities and complete records.
- **Numerical analysis:** an independent calculation, or a pinned established method
  with reviewed assumptions and discriminating fixtures. Check sample membership,
  effect direction, and intermediate quantities. Shared engines do not independently
  corroborate one another.
- **Equivalent outputs:** declare acceptable rooting, cluster-label permutations,
  or alignment alternatives; otherwise prescribe the method. Exclude underdetermined
  interpretations from automatic reward.

Define each numeric field's tolerance before student evaluation, using
`abs(actual - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference)` or a published interval.
Justify precision/rounding and check finite values, signs, units, missingness, and
duplicate IDs separately. Counts, coefficients, and p-values need different rules.
State threshold conventions; do not widen tolerances after failures.

All mandatory checks must pass for reward 1; otherwise a scored attempt gets 0.
Keep per-check diagnostics. Broken specifications (`invalid_task`) and `infra_error`
produce no training reward. Deliberately invalid input with a specified diagnostic
remains a valid, scoreable task.

Require references and accepted alternatives to pass; empty, malformed, and plausible
wrong outputs must fail. Mutations include reversed labels, dropped outcome classes,
pooled donors, shuffled IDs, transformed counts, wrong denominators, shifted
coordinates, ignored strand, and wrong variant alleles. Check row-permutation
invariance and copied answers across instances with different targets.

In the cohort experiment, reversed outcome labels passed an AIC-only grader because
AIC was unchanged. Check positive-class definitions, included patients, signed
effects, and predictions; vary PR/SD/PD recoding explicitly. Regrade affected
historical artifacts under a new verifier version while preserving original results.

Upstream tests require scrutiny: [SPAdes](https://github.com/ablab/spades/blob/808b87dade1300ecaa712429955ccba7bfb286f4/src/projects/spades/pipeline/spades_pipeline/supplemetary/check_test_script.py)
checks contig count/length, and [FastTree](https://github.com/morgannprice/fasttree/blob/a5a2723ea1e64faf3da7ea514521cfa348891add/CompareTree.pl)
documents rooted-tree limitations. pysam/SAMtools/HTSlib and pybedtools/BEDTools
share implementations. Strengthen rewards accordingly; schema or aggregate agreement
alone cannot establish biological correctness.

## Data separation and reproducible environments

Register source revisions, accessions, publications, hashes, terms, and derivations
before generation. Deduplicate exact artifacts and semantic equivalents; hash
differences do not prove biological independence. Keep generated tasks in one train
split and track entire lineages, including subsets, variants, perturbations, and
repairs, for deduplication and benchmark exclusion. Evaluation benchmarks and their
derivatives remain outside the training corpus. Resampling one dataset does not
separate its lineage; compositions inherit every parent's exclusions.

Exclusion groups include CompBioBench's `pbmc3k.h5ad`/`10x_pbmc68k_reduced.h5ad`,
BiomniBench-DA's GSE236581/GSE243013, BioAgent's HG001/NA12878 and ERR188297 fixtures,
the Zeisel cortex lineage used by Liu single-cell gimVI, and overlapping
BixBench/Verified-50 capsules. Treat shared reference genomes separately
from sample data and record both. For OOD decontamination, use permitted metadata
and policy-approved mechanisms without inspecting questions.

Package Harbor instructions, `task.toml`, inputs, and pinned Python, R/Bioconductor,
or sequence-CLI profiles. Pin tools, databases, locale, seeds, and threads. Isolate
answers/tests from solvers and check outputs with trusted dependencies. Repairs
also execute on fresh hidden inputs. Validate resources with reference runs.

## Internet policy

Default to **no public internet during synthetic-task attempts**. Stage inputs,
packages, reference data, and useful documentation beforehand. Online data origins
alone should not create a download requirement. Keep five attempts reproducible
and reserve their 30 minutes for the intended work.

Teach retrieval using a **frozen searchable catalog or local API**: select accessions,
assembly/transcript versions, or cohorts among competing records. Preserve meaningful
query/pagination behavior and verify IDs, versions, provenance, and analysis outputs.
Record retrieval skill and network mode explicitly.

Allow **live internet only when the target skill requires it**. Declare services,
bound calls/transfers, and archive requests/responses and versions. Respect service
limits such as [NCBI's](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25497/). Separate outages
from solver errors and report live tasks separately. Require a frozen executable
contract and offline verifier; exclude tasks without one. Existing benchmarks keep
their network rules; offline adaptations are named variants.

## Components to reuse

Reuse execution, packaging, and traces from Marin revision
`12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3`; add biology generators/contracts.

| Component | Use and boundary |
|---|---|
| [TaskTrove format](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3/experiments/post_training/tasktrove/task_format.py), [verifiers](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3/lib/tasktrove-verify/README.md) | Reuse Harbor layout, script/pytest execution, verdict statuses, and positive/negative checks. Add scientific mutations. Exclude judge mode and LLM routing. |
| [Curriculum](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3/experiments/post_training/task_curriculum/models.py), [trajectories](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trajectory.py) | Reuse capability/outcome/prerequisite/facet fields and archival. Add biological lineage; source-local instruction deduplication is insufficient. |
| [Backtranslation #7813](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7813) | Borrow repository discovery and instruction backtranslation. Its named `scientific_software.py`/`repo_backtranslation.py` are absent from this checkout, so use the inspected inventory without depending on that implementation or a full Stack scan. |
| [OpenThoughts-Agent, `3bd1917`](https://github.com/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts-Agent/tree/3bd1917e62c9d03d73063b433f5c442c279c0563/data/self_instruct) | Separate task/verifier authoring and executable packaging. A second model author is not an independent scientific reference. Review recipes and preinstall grader dependencies. |
| [SWE-smith, `9b74ac0`](https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-smith/tree/9b74ac08118a85c39c356802f7961893af73e07f) | Adapt mutation → failing test → repair to scientific defects and complete biological outputs. |
| [SERA, `1ca8673`](https://github.com/allenai/SERA/tree/1ca8673bd527b164dc9eb89841c96416ec8ce1a7) | Optional change-description/reconstruction pattern. Patch-overlap verification cannot establish biology correctness; exclude that filter from admission. |

## Later phase: teacher configuration and trace selection

The current work completes the executable task dataset first. This proposed trace
collection protocol is separate and is not a task-dataset acceptance requirement.

Use **GLM-5.3 with explicit `reasoning_effort: high`** as the proposed teacher.
[GLM documentation](https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3) supports high but defaults
to max; our choice remains a cost/quality hypothesis. Record model/weights,
tokenizer/template, serving configuration, temperature, and supported seeds.
Verify high reaches both request and rendered template using the
[vLLM recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/zai-org/GLM-5.3).

Start from the [Harbor #165 ceilings](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/165#issuecomment-5778903707):

```yaml
n_attempts: 5
agents:
  - name: terminus-2
    model_name: hosted_vllm/glm-5.3
    kwargs:
      model_info:
        max_input_tokens: 65536
        max_output_tokens: 32768
      llm_call_kwargs:
        max_tokens: 32768
        reasoning_effort: high
```

Align serving `max_model_len: 65536` and `max_gen_toks: 32768`: the context window
includes prompt and completion; reasoning counts toward output. Set episode
limits separately, including compaction calls. Test 131,072 context only with
serving support and measured throughput/memory. The inspected
[Marin driver](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py)
validates ordinary-call caps. Pin Harbor with [#193](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/193).
[#165's follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/165) reports
1/10 correct and eight two-hour timeouts; latency/compaction confound that result.
Remeasure current serving latency, truncation, execution, and compaction separately.

Cap each attempt at **30 minutes** (`agent.timeout_sec: 1800`) for every task;
measure setup/verifier time separately and redesign tasks that consistently exceed
it. Timed-out traces are ineligible for complete-trace SFT even if saved answers
score. Benchmarks retain their declared limits.

Request **five independent attempts per task**, each in a clean environment at a
fixed nonzero temperature, without earlier attempts or verifier feedback. Record
infrastructure retries separately. Retain all complete, deterministically passing
traces; deduplicate identical trajectories. Keep failures for inspection only.
Recovery within a successful trajectory is allowed.

Normalize weight per task within its scientific-workflow allocation, then sample its
passing traces. Report distinct solved IDs, retained traces, and the 0/5–5/5
distribution. Valid 0/5 tasks remain in the bank without SFT examples. Budget from
observed durations/tokens including failures; five attempts imply five attempts per
recipe at the one-task default. At a later 10,000 tasks, the ceiling is 50,000 attempts or
25,000 solver-hours, not an expected cost.

Export complete successful trajectories with the declared reasoning mode and
assistant loss mask; preserve tool interactions, remove hidden grading feedback,
and reject incomplete exports. Version tasks, graders, environments, models, and
exports; regrade after verifier defects. Test reward shortcuts before repeated RL.

## Inspecting tasks and synthetic trajectories

Provide a browsable corpus from the first tasks. Reuse
[TaskTrove's files](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3/infra/marina/apps/tasktrove/web/src/views/Task.vue)
and [EvalDash's trajectories](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/README.md),
excluding its optional LLM review. The corpus/attempt join, biology previews, and
review annotations require extensions; they are not an existing unified browser.

| View | Required capability |
|---|---|
| Corpus | Group by scientific workflow; filter skills, format profiles, source, input scale, network, lineage, 0/5–5/5, selection, cost, and failure. Show task/trace counts and reproducible sampling. All tasks are train. |
| Task | Exact prompt, native input previews and sizes, real/modified-real/simulated label, source accessions/checksums, reproducible subsetting, format conventions, contract, verifier, and reference/actual differences. Keep answer panels inaccessible to solvers. |
| ID coverage | Browse every permitted benchmark task ID and its workflow requirements, mapped recipes/examples, coverage status, execution evidence, and gaps. Filter by benchmark and component versus complete workflow; show total/eligible counts and exclusions. |
| Attempts | All five attempts including failures; full reasoning, commands, observations, recovery, compaction, timing/tokens, and per-check verdicts. Immutable revision links. |
| Review | Notes/flags for ambiguity, invalid biology, false passes/fails, duplication, or export defects. Notes never set reward; fixes create versions and trigger regrading. |

Inspect every selected task and exercise applicable null, invalid and boundary
cases separately, plus passing/failing attempts when available. At release,
review a fixed-seed stratified sample of up to 100 accepted traces and targeted
0/5, mixed-pass, short-success, and numerical boundary cases. Report random and
targeted defect rates separately. Quarantine defective recipe versions until repaired
and regraded. Use bounded previews and downloadable manifests/example bundles.

## Training comparisons and experiment records

| Question | Controlled comparison |
|---|---|
| Does biology data help? | Same student checkpoint: unchanged, general-terminal SFT, biology SFT; share any background mixture. Measure biology transfer and policy-permitted general-terminal retention. |
| Which authoring route helps? | Seeds, skills, and a 50:50 token mixture on common skill coverage. Report extra coverage/cost separately; treat repair tasks as a separate stratum. |
| Do short skills compose? | Short-only versus a matched-token mixture with dependent workflows, evaluated on compositional tasks in the separate benchmarks. |
| Does scale help? | Nested recipe-diverse task sets at constant exposure; use 2k/5k/full when available. A fixed-token comparison separates diversity from more compute. |

For matched comparisons, fix loss-bearing assistant tokens, starting checkpoint,
optimizer, harness, tools, and evaluation budgets; report context tokens and compute.
Record reasoning/template, context, summarization, and stopping settings. Show
individual seeds when replication is too small for useful uncertainty estimates.

Report ID results separately by benchmark/adapter, with per-workflow, study-design
and composition scores where supported. Use policy-permitted ID results for
development and freeze choices before policy-governed OOD evaluation.
Estimate paired uncertainty by independent
lineage, grouping sibling questions and repeated attempts.

Report attempted, scored, successful, invalid-task, and infrastructure-failure counts.
Under #9193, eligible agent timeouts/context/turn limits/nonzero exits with completed
verifier results are scoreable; setup, whole-trial, export, and verifier failures
are unscored. Use the common scored set for paired comparisons and disclose missingness.

Record admission rates, coverage, success by attempt, verifier defects, scientific
errors, trace lengths, runtime, and cost per accepted task/trace, including rejects
and amortized authoring/environment costs. Preserve recipe/lineage manifests, pins,
references/adversarial fixtures, task/trace artifacts, SFT configs, and paired results.
The issue body holds the design/conclusion; comments hold run evidence and decisions.
Source inspection does not establish runtime validity or training gain.

## Maintained catalogs

The [task catalog](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-task-catalog.md) contains all
50 inspected repositories with pinned evidence and verification limitations, the
full skill inventory, and format profiles. The vendored
[original adoption inventory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/computational_biology_bioinformatics_packages.md)
preserves all 50 repositories' downloads, stars, canonical-paper citations, and
metric caveats as reported on 2026-07-28. The catalog also preserves additional
analysis/benchmark references and attribution/licensing notes. Update the catalog
alongside recipes; use commit permalinks for released snapshots and the branch link
for current authoring. [Generator documentation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/docs/experiments/bio-tasks.md)
lists implemented coverage and build/inspection instructions.

The [biological source manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/data_sources.json)
and [task-level index](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_coverage.json)
link the [per-benchmark inventories](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_tasks)
and [agentic source policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-task-generators/experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/benchmark_sources.json).
Maintain these files alongside the code. Keep assessed component mappings and independently
validated workflows distinct, retaining unmapped and restricted items in the denominator.

comments.body:
🤖 The pilot is idle with no GPU jobs running. Both planned 10-step attempts stopped in tiny-model preflight before student loading. Working Snowball SFT precedents now include a report on the same September 21 checkpoint, but the exact training path is not yet matched to this pilot. Resume after obtaining a reproducible working revision/configuration and reviewing the remaining differences. The baseline remains 0/1; the earlier four-step model’s incoherent evaluation remains ungraded. The [detailed experiment record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5778284554) contains configuration and artifacts.

<details>
<summary>Pilot artifacts, limitation, and next step — September 23, 2026</summary>

- **Hold further GPU runs; closer precedent identified (September 23):** The user supplied the text of [Harshit Varma’s report](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1374989195109466122/1552425627976474645). It continues the same `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21` checkpoint on filtered AgentTrove plus GLM-5.3 RST successes: 63,504 rows, two epochs/722 steps, batch 64, sequence 32,768, `5e-5` AdamH with cosine and 3% warmup. Reported held-out NLL improves 1.094 → 0.909 and parse-fail turns fall 67% → 25%, while premature completion, recovery, and long-context behavior regress. This supports a functioning SFT/serving path for our student, not a claim of improved overall TB2 performance. The screenshot does not give hardware, code revision, or the exact optimizer class.

  The completed four-step biology pilot used ordinary Adam at constant `5e-5`; the unexecuted ten-step plan uses ordinary Adam with cosine and no warmup. [Marin’s AdamH implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/optim/adamh.py) preserves matrix norms and uses separate parameter groups, so equal nominal learning rates do not imply equivalent updates. This is a material difference to review, not an established explanation for the earlier incoherent model or the preflight NaNs. The latter occurred before any optimizer update.

  [Luke’s pinned launch record](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/d152f86a58e8619a988361e1502f9e55) is a separate reproducible precedent: `lukedhlee/vista-snowball-sft@23d8fda7`, Grug trainer/AdamH, 16 × 4 GH200s, EP8, batch 64, sequence 32,768, and a different Stage-3 starting model. It cannot be substituted for Harshit’s unspecified setup without checking those differences. Further GPU submissions are on hold with the user’s agreement; preserve the 31 traces, baseline, and failed-run evidence. The resume condition is an exact successful training/export configuration, not a merge flag alone.

- **Working precedents and revised recommendation (September 23, 21:15 UTC):** [PR #9331](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9331) reports completed one-update Snowball SFT followed by FinanceBench evaluation: baseline 26/50, task-only 27/50, curriculum 23/50. Those results use an earlier unpacked, assistant-masked path; the PR explicitly distinguishes the later packed/full-text recipe, which has not been rerun on H100s. [Issue #9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) separately documents a 64-H100 run at step 135 with a usable HF export despite a final checkpoint rewrite error. Our two failed preflights establish a problem in the tested configuration, not a general Snowball SFT blocker. comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
🤖 **Data:** The mix includes 95.6M tokens of GLM-5.3 compaction summaries, whose source prompt asks for objectives, completed and active work, blockers, and next moves.

**Evidence:** In one check, a workshop summary retains the budget, venue constraints, completed registration form, and unresolved decisions. A fresh chat uses that exact summary to compute the remaining budget and next action correctly. Summarization across varied tasks remains unmeasured.

- The selected behavior has explicit evaluation criteria for unnecessary verbosity, premature answers, and task success.
- The cold-start recipe records the selected design or the reason no design is ready.

comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
🤖 **Data:** The mix includes 1.37B tokens of `reasoning_off` and 1.19B of `reasoning_on` instruction chat; normalization sets the thinking mode from analysis messages for all input data.

**Evidence:** Model does not emit thinking tokens when reasoning is turned off and reliably emits reasoning when thinking is turned on in one-of checks on Chat UI. Thinking is on for all chat evals in current eval policy and, as such, the model always thinks.

comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
🤖 **Data:** The mix includes 95.6M tokens of GLM-5.3 compaction summaries. No selected source is dedicated to continuation from a summary.

**Evidence:** Given its own workshop summary in a fresh chat, the model preserves completed work and computes the remaining budget correctly. Given a conflicting Q2 summary, it asks for verification instead of inventing a figure, but omits the verified Q1 baseline. These are two one-off checks, so continuation from varied summaries remains weakly verified.

spillover_issues.body:
Refine cold-start SFT supervision for reasoning across science, mathematics, legal, and medical contexts, and for basic agentic tool use. This is a child of #8089.

Existing work in #7321 and #7743 provides relevant SFT data, serving, and agentic-evaluation evidence, but does not establish a general cold-start recipe for these capabilities.

Done when:

- Candidate cross-domain thinking and tool-use data are identified with immutable revisions and clear licensing/provenance.
- Acceptance evaluations cover each domain and basic tool selection, execution, and response integration.
- The cold-start recipe records the selected data and evaluation contract.

comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
🤖 **Data:** The mix includes 3.04B tokens of `nemotron_sft_v3/science_v2/vendor`, 2.03B of `math_v4`, and agent, tool, terminal, and SWE traces. Nemotron SFT v3 has legal & medical data.

**Evidence:** One-off science, math, fictional contract, and educational diagnostic-test answers are correct. A Python tool call and a five-call simulated ShellSim repair both lead to useful final answers. A separate legal answer misstates the notice date but uses reasoning.

comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
🤖 **Data:** The mix includes 9.51M tokens of GLM-5.3 format completions and additional instruction-following chat.

**Evidence:** One-off checks produce exact JSON, an integer-only answer, a two-sentence answer, and three bullets as requested. A long-form answer uses the requested headings but contains invalid counterexamples; its follow-up has no final answer. Format and correctness need separate acceptance measurements.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Establish a versioned cold-start SFT recipe that runs immediately after pretraining cool-down. The recipe should produce a model with the core capabilities needed by Marin's post-training and evaluation workflows.

The initial competency set is:

- Chat-template adherence and basic instruction following.
- Think blocks.
- Thinking across science, mathematics, legal, and medical contexts.
- Adaptive thinking effort.
- Model-name responses.
- Basic agentic tool use.
- Answer-format hardening.
- Task summarization.
- Resuming a task from a summary.

Related preceding work: #7321 and #7743.

Research issues:

- #8093: adaptive thinking effort.
- #8094: model-name response behavior.
- #8092: answer-format hardening.
- #8095: task summarization.
- #8091: resume tasks from summaries.
- #8090: cross-domain thinking and basic agentic tool use.

Done when:

- A recipe version identifies its parent checkpoint, tokenizer and chat template, data mixture and immutable revisions, training configuration, and export contract.
- The recipe has acceptance evaluations for every listed competency, with recorded baseline comparisons and failure criteria.
- The recipe can be run after a pretraining cool-down without experiment-specific manual wiring.
- The selected recipe and its evidence are documented in the repository.
